subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should builtin memory-core add durable checkpoint/resume for forced/full reindex operations, and should that behavior be automatic or exposed through memorySearch config/status?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes durable memory generation semantics and may add public configuration or status behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Sponsor automatic resume
options.body: Implement resumable full reindex by default while preserving all-or-nothing publish semantics and adding status/tests for incomplete generations.

options.title: Make resume opt-in
options.body: Add a documented memorySearch checkpoint/resume option with proof for both default compatibility and opt-in behavior.

options.title: Defer checkpointing
options.body: Keep all-or-nothing rebuilds for now and focus narrower work on retry, metadata repair, stale-shadow cleanup, and clearer operator status.

recommendation.title: Sponsor automatic resume
recommendation.body: Implement resumable full reindex by default while preserving all-or-nothing publish semantics and adding status/tests for incomplete generations.

likelyOwner.reason: He has strong visible history on the memory-core reindex architecture and prior issue-review context for this exact item.
